mistakes.why: End-range shoulder extension loads the front capsule and the pec tendon.

mistakes.name: Shoulders shrug up
mistakes.looks: Shoulders rise toward the ears, neck looks short.
mistakes.fix: Push the bars down, shoulders away from ears.
mistakes.why: The shoulder blade loses its depressed, stable position.

mistakes.name: Elbows flare out
mistakes.looks: Elbows point to the sides as you go down.
mistakes.fix: Elbows back, hands under them.
mistakes.why: More abduction and rotation at the bottom shifts the work from the triceps to the shoulder.

safety: Shoulder pain at the bottom: shorten the range or use a dip machine or band.
Bench dips put the shoulder in more extension than bar dips; skip them if the front of the shoulder hurts.
Add weight only once you can do 10-12 clean bar dips.

variants.change: Lean forward about 30-45°, elbows can open a little: more chest.
Trunk near upright, elbows tight: more triceps.
Rings move: peak triceps activity like bar dips, but more stabiliser muscles work; turn the rings out at the top.
Weight on a belt or between the feet; same form.
Knee pad, counterweight or band helps you up: same arm path.
Seated dip machine: same arm path, trunk supported.

subtypes.name: Bench dip
subtypes.change: Hands behind you on a bench or chair, hips just in front, legs out. Lower by bending the elbows.

subtypes.name: Scapula dip
subtypes.change: Arms stay straight; only the shoulders move: sink up toward your ears, then push down tall.

subtypes.name: Dip hold
subtypes.change: Hold the top or the bottom position still, shoulders down.

subtypes.name: Korean dip
subtypes.change: Hands on a bar behind your back: very large shoulder extension; advanced only.

motion.basis: Bottom position measured in mckenzie2022b (bar dip): shoulder extension 68 ± 11°, abduction 31 ± 4°, elbow flexion 115 ± 9°, thoracic lean 37 ± 10°, external rotation 9 ± 14°. Bench dip needs more shoulder extension (mckenzie2022a); its angles are estimates. Scapula was not measured in any study: values are estimates (depressed at the top, slight downward rotation and anterior drift as the shoulder extends).

families.name: Elliptical
families.pattern: Standing gait on two pedals that trace an oval: feet never leave the pedals, arms push and pull the handles opposite the legs.
setup: Step on with the pedals still, holding the fixed bars.
Whole foot on the pedal, toes forward, feet hip width.
Then move your hands to the moving handles at chest height.

steps.text: Right pedal forward and up, left pedal back; left hand pulls, right hand pushes.
Press the right pedal down and back through the whole foot.
Switch: left pedal forward, right pedal back.
Press the left pedal down and back. Keep a smooth, even rhythm.

cues.cue: Stand tall over the pedals, shoulders over hips.
cues.why: Leaning on the rails takes body weight off the legs and lowers the work done.

cues.cue: Keep the whole foot down; let the heel lift only a little at the back.
cues.why: Up on the toes loads the calves and can numb the feet.

cues.cue: Knees track over the toes, soft, never locked.
cues.why: Elliptical knee motion stays more bent than in walking; locking loses that.

cues.cue: Push and pull the handles; do not just rest on them.
cues.why: Active arms add upper-body work and raise the energy cost.

families.breathing: Breathe steadily through the nose and mouth in time with your stride.

tempo.note: About 50-70 revolutions a minute; harder by resistance or incline, not just speed.

mistakes.name: Leaning on the rails
mistakes.looks: Elbows locked on the bars, body bent forward, weight in the hands.
mistakes.fix: Hands light on the moving handles, chest up.
mistakes.why: Supporting body weight through the arms cuts the leg work and calories, and rounds the back.

mistakes.name: Up on the toes
mistakes.looks: Heels lift high off the pedals the whole time.
mistakes.fix: Drive through the heel and midfoot.
mistakes.why: Calves tire early and feet go numb.

mistakes.name: Too fast, no resistance
mistakes.looks: Legs spin with no load and the body bobs.
mistakes.fix: Add resistance until each push feels firm.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the work and the effort drops.

safety: Step on and off only when the pedals are still.
Knee pain: lower the incline and keep the knees soft.

variants.change: Moderate effort: about 5.0 MET (02048).
Vigorous effort: about 9.0 MET (02049).
Hands off: arms swing as in walking, more balance work.

motion.basis: Direction of differences from walking (more hip and pelvic motion, knee curve shifted to more flexion) from damiano2011 and lu2007 (cadence about 52 rpm in that study); the degree values are estimates.

families.name: Face pull
families.pattern: High pull to the face with external rotation: elbows pull out and back at shoulder height, then the hands turn back beside the ears.
setup: Set a rope at about eye height; hold the ends with thumbs pointing back toward you.
Step back until the arms are straight and the weight is off the stack.
Stand tall, feet hip width or staggered, ribs down.

steps.text: Arms straight forward at shoulder height, shoulder blades slightly spread.
Pull the rope toward your face, elbows high and wide, shoulder blades squeezing back.
Finish by turning your hands back so they end beside your ears, knuckles up, like a double biceps pose.
Reverse the path slowly until your arms are straight.

cues.cue: Elbows at shoulder height, pointing out to the sides.
cues.why: Pulling with the arms out at the side and turning out is the position where the rear delt and middle trapezius are most active.

cues.cue: Finish with your hands beside your ears, thumbs back.
cues.why: Adding external rotation at the end works the infraspinatus and lower trapezius; palms-up pulls raised both.

cues.cue: Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down, not up.
cues.why: Exercises with low upper-trap to mid and lower trap ratios are preferred for scapular balance.

cues.cue: Stand tall; do not lean back to finish the rep.
cues.why: Leaning turns it into a row and uses the body weight instead of the rear shoulder.

cues.cue: Use a light weight you can hold at the end for one second.
cues.why: Face pulls give rear-delt force similar to a bent-over rear raise, so heavy loads are not needed.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you pull, in as you return.

tempo.note: Pull in 1 second, hold the end 1 second, return in 2.

mistakes.name: Elbows drop
mistakes.looks: The elbows fall to the ribs and the rope comes to the chest, like a row.
mistakes.fix: Raise the anchor and keep the elbows level with the shoulders.
mistakes.why: With the elbows low the lats and biceps take over and the rear shoulder works less.

mistakes.name: No turn-out at the end
mistakes.looks: The hands stop in front of the face, forearms pointing forward.
mistakes.fix: Pull the ends apart and turn your hands back beside your ears.
mistakes.why: Skipping the rotation misses most of the rotator cuff work.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders rise toward the ears as the rope comes in.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load; shoulders down first, then pull.
mistakes.why: The upper trapezius takes over from the middle and lower trapezius.

safety: Shoulder pain at the end: stop the rotation short and keep the elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Use a rope or band so the hands can move apart freely.

variants.change: Palms up grip: more infraspinatus and lower trapezius.
Seated or kneeling: less trunk lean available, stricter.
One arm: trunk resists twisting; same arm path.
Lying face up under the cable: the back is supported, same arm path.
Body-weight version leaning back on straps: harder as the feet move forward.
Bent over with dumbbells: trunk near horizontal, elbows pull out and up, then turn out.

metrics.label: Elbow height
metrics.good: 75-95 at the end (elbows at shoulder level)

motion.basis: End position matches the prone horizontal abduction with external rotation tested in reinold2004 and ekstrom2003; hand position effect from fukunaga2022 (band pull-apart). Scapular upward rotation near 20° at 85° abduction from ludewig2009 rhythm, estimated. Few studies test the face pull itself (zhu2025, model-based), so joint angles are mainly coaching convention.

families.name: Foam rolling
families.pattern: Self-massage: body weight presses one muscle onto a foam roller or ball while you roll slowly along its length.
setup: Place the roller under the muscle you want to treat, across the muscle's length.
Use hands and feet to set how much body weight goes onto the roller.
Pick a pressure of about 5-7 out of 10: firm, never sharp.

steps.text: Roll slowly along the muscle, about 2-4 seconds from one end to the other.
Roll back the same way. Pause a few breaths on a tender spot if you like.

cues.cue: Slow: 2-4 seconds for each pass along the muscle.
cues.why: Prescriptions with the biggest range-of-motion gains used 2-4 s per roll.

cues.cue: 30-120 seconds per muscle, 1-3 rounds.
cues.why: That volume gave the largest range gains; short bouts of 5-10 s already help a little.

cues.cue: Use it in your warm-up or after training for soreness.
cues.why: Before exercise it gives small gains in flexibility and sprint; after, it slightly reduces soreness.

cues.cue: Firm but bearable; breathe and let the muscle soften.
cues.why: Effects are mostly from nervous-system and pain changes, not from breaking up fascia, so more pain is not better.

cues.cue: Keep your trunk braced and roll the muscle, not the joint or bone.
cues.why: Bony points and joints get pressure with no benefit.

families.breathing: Slow, easy breaths; breathe out as you sink into a tender spot.

tempo.note: 2-4 s per pass, 30-120 s per muscle. Speed itself matters little: slow and fast rolling lowered stiffness about equally.

mistakes.name: Rolling too fast
mistakes.looks: Quick back-and-forth sawing over the roller.
mistakes.fix: Slow down to about 3 seconds per pass.
mistakes.why: Fast passes make it hard to relax and to control pressure; the best-studied dose is 2-4 s per roll.

mistakes.name: Low back sags or arches
mistakes.looks: On the upper back the hips drop and the low back arches over the roller.
mistakes.fix: Lift the hips, brace, hands behind the head.
mistakes.why: Rolls the lumbar spine instead of the muscle.

mistakes.name: Rolling over joints or bone
mistakes.looks: The roller runs over the knee, the shin bone, or the spine's bony points.
mistakes.fix: Stop a hand's width short of the joint.
mistakes.why: Pressure on bone and joints gives no benefit and can bruise.

safety: Skip areas with bruises, open wounds, varicose veins, recent fractures or swelling.
Do not roll the front of the neck or press hard into the belly; use a soft ball and light pressure on the abdomen.
Blood clot history, blood thinners or osteoporosis: ask your doctor first.
Sharp, burning or tingling pain means stop.

variants.change: Ball: smaller, more focused pressure; roll small circles rather than long passes.
Bar or stick roller: you press it on with your hands; same speed and time.
One leg on the roller, the other crossed over: more pressure.

subtypes.name: Neck and upper trapezius
subtypes.change: Lying face up with a soft ball or roller under the back of the neck; small nods and turns, light pressure only.

subtypes.name: Abdomen and hip flexors (ball)
subtypes.change: Face down with a soft ball under the belly or front of the hip; slow breaths, gentle pressure, tiny movements.

subtypes.name: Lats and side of the back
subtypes.change: Side lying, roller under the armpit, bottom arm overhead; roll from the armpit to the bottom of the ribs.

subtypes.name: Chest and front shoulder
subtypes.change: Face down with a ball under the chest just below the collarbone, or lying lengthwise on a roller with arms open; small strokes toward the shoulder.

subtypes.name: Back of the shoulder
subtypes.change: Lying face up, ball under the shoulder blade or back of the shoulder; reach the arm across the body and back.

subtypes.name: Forearms, biceps, triceps
subtypes.change: Arm on the roller or ball on a table or wall; roll from wrist to elbow (forearm) or elbow to shoulder (upper arm).

subtypes.name: Lower back (ball, gentle)
subtypes.change: Use a ball beside (not on) the spine, or a roller only on the muscles to the side; small slow movements. Do not lie with a roller across the lower back.

subtypes.name: Upper back and thoracic
subtypes.match: upper back|thoracic|middle back|rhomboids|trapezius lower|around the world|back stretch|back rotation|kneeling upper back
subtypes.change: Roller across the mid back, hands behind the head, hips lifted; roll from the bottom of the shoulder blades to the top. Thoracic extension: hips down, arch gently over the roller.

subtypes.name: Glutes, piriformis, TFL
subtypes.change: Sit on the roller, cross one ankle over the other knee and lean onto that buttock; roll small passes. TFL: face down and turned slightly, roller at the front-side of the hip.

subtypes.name: Inner thigh
subtypes.change: Face down on the forearms, one knee out to the side with the inner thigh on the roller; roll from near the knee toward the groin.

subtypes.name: Hamstrings
subtypes.change: Sit with the roller under the back of the thighs, hands behind you, hips lifted; roll from the sit bones to just above the knee.

subtypes.name: Quads and outer thigh
subtypes.change: Face down on the forearms in a plank, roller under the front of the thighs; roll from the hip to just above the knee. Turn a little to reach the outer thigh.

subtypes.name: Calves, shins, peroneals, foot
subtypes.change: Calf: sit with the roller under the calves, hands behind, hips lifted; roll from the ankle to below the knee. Shin and peroneals: kneel or side-lie with the roller beside, not on, the shin bone. Foot: stand and roll a ball under the arch.

motion.basis: Default keyframes: upper-back rolling. Dose (2-4 s per pass, 30-120 s per set, 1-3 sets) from behm2020; speed effects from wilke2019 and sezik2024; 5-10 s effects from sullivan2013; up to 2 min on the hamstrings gave no range gain in couture2015. Body angles are estimates of the usual positions; the roller position along the muscle is shown by moving the body with the legs or arms. Subtypes are listed most specific first; the first match wins.

families.name: Front raise
families.pattern: Shoulder flexion: straight-ish arms lift forward to about shoulder height and lower again.
setup: Stand tall, weights in front of your thighs.
Palms facing your legs or each other, soft bend in the elbows.
Brace: ribs down, knees soft.

steps.text: Lift the arms forward and up, keeping the elbows soft.
Stop at shoulder height, hands about level with your eyes at most.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.

cues.cue: Up to shoulder height.
cues.why: The front delt does most of the work up to about 90°; higher brings in the traps and serratus to rotate the shoulder blade.

cues.cue: Thumbs up or palms in feels best on the shoulder.
cues.why: Thumb-up (full can) arm positions load the cuff without the turned-in empty-can position.

cues.cue: No lean back or hip swing.
cues.why: Leaning back turns it into a swing and loads the lower back.

cues.cue: Shoulders down, let the shoulder blades glide naturally.
cues.why: The shoulder blade rotates up about 1° for every 2° of arm raise; shrugging adds upper-trap work instead.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Slow, light weight.

mistakes.name: Leaning back and swinging
mistakes.looks: The trunk rocks back and the hips push forward to lift the weight.
mistakes.fix: Stand still with a lighter weight, or sit or chest-support.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the work and the lower back arches.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders hike up as the arms rise.
mistakes.fix: Shoulders down, stop at shoulder height.
mistakes.why: The upper trap takes the load.

mistakes.name: Elbows bend
mistakes.looks: Elbows bend more and more and the weight curls up.
mistakes.fix: Fix the elbow bend at about 10-20°.
mistakes.why: Shortens the lever and adds biceps.

safety: Shoulder pain: stop below 80° and use thumbs up.
Use light weights; the arm is a long lever.

variants.change: Both hands on one implement: palms down for a bar, palms in for a plate.
Cable from behind between the legs: tension at the bottom.
One arm: hold the trunk still.
Full can: arms 30° out from the front in the scapular plane, thumbs up.

variants.when: lateral to front|front and lateral|6 ways
variants.change: Combined raise: alternate side and front paths.
Palms up: a bit more biceps and upper chest.
Hold the arms at shoulder height.

subtypes.name: Front raise to overhead
subtypes.change: Keep raising past shoulder height until the arms are overhead.

subtypes.name: Incline chest-supported raise
subtypes.change: Lying face down on an incline bench about 45°, arms hang and lift forward to line up with the body.

subtypes.name: Lying front raise
subtypes.change: Lying on your back (bench or floor), lift the weight from over the thighs to over the chest: hardest at the start.

subtypes.name: Seated front raise
subtypes.change: Seated on a bench, no leg drive: same arm path.

motion.basis: Scapular upward rotation from the flexion ratio of about 2:1 and 46° total over full flexion in mcclure2001 (about 28° at 90° including a resting value, estimate); slight protraction during flexion is an estimate. Arm angles are by design (stop at shoulder height). Muscle emphasis from coratella2020 (frontal raise gave the highest anterior deltoid activity).

families.name: Glute kickback
families.pattern: Single-leg hip extension: one leg drives back from the hip while the trunk and pelvis stay still.
setup: On hands and knees: hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
Working knee bent about 90°, foot flexed.
Brace your belly so the low back stays still.

steps.text: Drive the heel up and back toward the ceiling, knee still bent.
Stop when the thigh is level with your body.
Squeeze the glute for a second.
Lower the knee back under the hip without touching down.

cues.cue: Keep the knee bent 90° or more.
cues.why: A bent knee slackens the hamstrings so the glute does more of the work.

cues.cue: Back flat like a table; stop when the thigh is level.
cues.why: Lifting higher comes from arching the low back, not from the hip.

cues.cue: Hips square to the floor, do not twist open.
cues.why: Rotation lets other muscles move the leg.

cues.cue: Slow, with a pause at the top.
cues.why: The glute tends to switch on last in prone hip extension; a pause gives it time to work.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you kick back, in as you return.

tempo.note: Controlled; no swinging.

mistakes.name: Low back arches
mistakes.looks: The leg goes higher than the body and the low back sinks.
mistakes.fix: Brace, and stop when the thigh is level.
mistakes.why: Range comes from the spine; the glute does less.

mistakes.name: Hip twists open
mistakes.looks: The working hip lifts and turns toward the ceiling.
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor.
mistakes.why: Rotation takes the glute max out of a pure hip extension.

mistakes.name: Knee straightens
mistakes.looks: The leg kicks out straight as it rises.
mistakes.fix: Hold the knee angle, push the heel to the ceiling.
mistakes.why: A straight knee lets the hamstrings take over.

safety: Wrist pain on all fours: use fists or forearms on a bench.
Low back pain: keep the range short and the trunk braced.

variants.change: Load pulls the foot forward: the start (hip bent) is harder, the top easier with a band.
Knee straight: longer lever, more hamstring.
Leg goes back and out: more glute medius.
Machine pad on the foot or thigh; same hip action, fixed path.
Hands or trunk on a bench: less wrist load, same hip action.

subtypes.name: Standing cable / band kickback
subtypes.match: standing|cable kickback|cable straight leg|band kickback|band hip extension|bent-over hip extension|bent over hip extension|long lever
subtypes.change: Standing, hands on a support, trunk tipped slightly forward; the leg goes from in front of the hip to behind it.

subtypes.name: Straight-leg kickback
subtypes.change: On all fours with the working knee straight.

subtypes.name: Prone hip extension
subtypes.change: Lying face down, knee bent 90°, lift the thigh off the floor a few degrees.

motion.basis: Quadruped bent-knee kickback (right leg working). Knee at or above 60-90° from kwon2013 and jeon2016; other angles are estimates from the table-top position (trunk 90, support hip and knee 90).

families.name: Hanging leg raise
families.pattern: Hanging from a bar (or supported in a captain's chair), the knees or straight legs lift and the pelvis curls up toward the ribs.
setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms, hands shoulder width, or rest your forearms in a captain's chair.
Pull your shoulders slightly down so you don't hang loose.
Legs together, still, no swing.

steps.text: Raise your knees (or straight legs) to hip height.
Keep going: tilt your pelvis up so your knees rise toward your chest.
Lower under control until your legs hang straight, without swinging.

cues.cue: Curl the pelvis up, don't just lift the legs.
cues.why: Hanging knee-ups were among the top exercises for rectus abdominis and internal oblique activity, but only when the pelvis curls.

cues.cue: No swing: pause at the bottom.
cues.why: Momentum takes over the lift and reduces abdominal work.

cues.cue: Shoulders down, lats on.
cues.why: An active hang steadies the trunk; the lats work hard in this lift.

cues.cue: Bend the knees to make it easier, straighten to make it harder.
cues.why: Straight legs make a longer lever and a harder exercise.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 second, lower in 2, pause before the next rep.

mistakes.name: Swinging
mistakes.looks: The body rocks back and forth and the legs fly up.
mistakes.fix: Pause dead still at the bottom of each rep.
mistakes.why: Momentum, not the abs, lifts the legs.

mistakes.name: Legs stop at hip height
mistakes.looks: Thighs reach level but the pelvis never tilts up.
mistakes.fix: Keep lifting: knees toward the chest.
mistakes.why: Without the pelvic curl it is mostly a hip flexor lift.

mistakes.name: Shoulders shrug to the ears
mistakes.looks: The head sinks between the arms.
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulders down before you lift.
mistakes.why: A passive hang strains the shoulder and lets the trunk wobble.

safety: Shoulder pain: use a captain's chair or ab straps instead of a hang.
Low back pain: start with bent knees and stop at hip height.

variants.change: Bent knees: easier, shorter lever.
Straight legs: harder; toes-to-bar brings the feet up to the hands.
Forearms on pads: no grip demand, less shoulder load.
Knees lift to one side or circle: more oblique work.
Load at the feet makes the lever heavier.

subtypes.name: Toes to bar
subtypes.change: Legs keep rising until the feet (or knees) touch the bar; the trunk leans back.

subtypes.name: Captain's chair
subtypes.change: Back against the pad, forearms on the arm rests; same leg path.

motion.basis: Default is the bent-knee hanging raise. All angles estimated from the technique; activation ranking from escamilla2006 and mcgill2015.

families.name: High knees and butt kicks
families.pattern: Running in place with an exaggerated leg action: thighs up to hip height (high knees) or heels up to the glutes (butt kicks).
setup: Stand tall, feet hip width, on the balls of your feet.
Elbows bent about 90°, hands relaxed.

steps.text: Drive one knee up to hip height, the foot under the knee.
Land softly on the ball of the foot under your hip.
Drive the other knee as the arms swing opposite.

cues.cue: Stand tall; do not lean back to lift the knees.
cues.why: Leaning back lets the hip flexors pull on the lower back instead of lifting the thigh.

cues.cue: Quick, light contacts on the balls of the feet.
cues.why: Short ground contact is the point of these running drills.

cues.cue: Thigh to hip height, ankle flexed (toes up).
cues.why: Full knee lift trains the hip flexors through range; a flexed ankle readies the foot to land.

cues.cue: Arms pump forward and back, opposite the legs.
cues.why: Opposite arm swing balances the trunk rotation.

families.breathing: Steady, quick breaths in rhythm with the steps.

tempo.note: About 3-4 steps a second for drills; slower marches for warm-ups.

mistakes.name: Leaning back
mistakes.looks: Shoulders behind the hips as the knees rise.
mistakes.fix: Chest tall, slightly forward.
mistakes.why: Lower back arches and the drill loses its running shape.

mistakes.name: Low knees
mistakes.looks: Thighs stay well below hip height.
mistakes.fix: Slow down until the thigh reaches level.
mistakes.why: Turns into jogging in place with less hip work.

mistakes.name: Heavy heel landings
mistakes.looks: Loud thuds, heels hit the floor.
mistakes.fix: Land on the forefoot, quiet feet.
mistakes.why: Higher impact on shins and knees.

safety: Low impact: march the knees up instead of hopping.

variants.change: No Compendium code for these drills; vigorous calisthenics 7.5 MET (02020) is the closest.
Easy marching or jogging in place: about 4.8 MET (12025).
Skipping, forward: about 11.5 MET (12600).

subtypes.name: High knees
subtypes.change: Default keyframes. Wall version: hands on a wall, body leaning 30°.

subtypes.name: Butt kicks
subtypes.change: Thigh stays near vertical; the heel flicks up to the glutes.

subtypes.name: Skips
subtypes.change: Step-hop on each foot with a high knee; travels forward.

subtypes.name: High knee walk
subtypes.change: Slow walking version, one foot always down, can hold a support.

motion.basis: No kinematic study found for these drills; angles are estimates. Cues are coaching convention (NSCA).

families.name: High pull and pulls
families.pattern: Explosive hip and knee extension with a shrug, then the elbows lead the weight up to chest height. No catch.
setup: Clean-width grip (snatch-wide for a snatch-grip pull), arms straight.
Stand tall with the bar at mid-thigh, or start from the floor for a sumo pull.
Shoulders slightly over the bar, back flat, chest up.

steps.text: Hinge so the bar slides to just above your knees, knees steady.
Knees and hips move forward under the bar as the torso rises.
Drive hips, knees and ankles straight and shrug hard.
Elbows lead the bar up close to your body to chest height.
Lower the bar to your thighs, softening the knees.

cues.cue: Jump first, then pull.
cues.why: Lower body extension produces the power; jump shrug and high pull both make more power than the hang power clean.

cues.cue: Stay tall: do not dip to reach the bar.
cues.why: Bending the knees again to meet the bar at chest height is the main error in the high pull.

cues.cue: Elbows high and out, no higher than your shoulders.
cues.why: Keeping the bar at chest height avoids pinching the shoulder at the top.

cues.cue: Bar close to your body.
cues.why: A close bar keeps the pull vertical and efficient.

cues.cue: Flat back in the hinge.
cues.why: Protects the lower back as load increases.

families.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the hinge, out once the bar is back down.

tempo.note: Explosive up, controlled return.

mistakes.name: Dipping under
mistakes.looks: Knees bend again as the bar reaches the chest.
mistakes.fix: Finish tall on your toes; use a lighter load.
mistakes.why: It turns the pull into a sloppy catch and cuts the extension.

mistakes.name: Arms do the work
mistakes.looks: Hips and knees barely move; the bar is rowed up.
mistakes.fix: Drive the floor away and shrug before the arms bend.
mistakes.why: Without the jump it becomes an upright row and loses its power training.

mistakes.name: Elbows too high
mistakes.looks: The bar comes up past the collarbone with elbows above the shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Stop the bar at nipple to chest height.
mistakes.why: Arm raise far above 90° with inward rotation can pinch the shoulder.

safety: Shoulder pain: stop at a jump shrug (no arm pull).
Sumo deadlift high pull from the floor: keep the back flat; it is common in conditioning workouts when tired, so cap reps.

variants.change: No arm pull: jump and shrug, land softly with bent knees. Highest power of the three hang derivatives.
From the floor, finish with extension and shrug only; loads may exceed the clean or snatch max.
Wide stance, narrow grip inside the knees, start from the floor.
One bell held in both hands between wide feet.
Rope from a low pulley; keep the jump small and the pull smooth.
Dumbbells at the thighs, elbows lead up and out.

subtypes.name: Sumo deadlift high pull
subtypes.change: Wide stance with toes out, narrow grip, pull from the floor.

subtypes.name: Jump shrug
subtypes.change: Same hang and extension, leave the floor with a shrug, arms stay straight.

metrics.label: Knee bend when the bar reaches the chest

motion.basis: Technique and the dipping error from suchomel2015; power ranking of hang derivatives from suchomel2014 and suchomel2017a. Joint angles are estimates from coaching descriptions, not measured values.

families.name: Hip abduction
families.pattern: Leg moves out to the side against resistance, lying, seated, standing or stepping, to train the side hip.
setup: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent for support, top leg straight in line with your body.
Stack your hips: the top hip directly over the bottom one, not rolled back.
Toes of the top leg point forward, not up.

steps.text: Top leg resting on the bottom one, hips stacked.
Raise the straight leg up and slightly back, heel leading.
Stop at about 35-45°, hold a second.
Lower slowly without letting the leg rest.

cues.cue: Keep your hips stacked; do not roll back.
cues.why: Rolling back turns the lift into hip flexion, which uses the front hip muscles instead of the glute medius.

cues.cue: Toes forward, heel leads, leg slightly behind you.
cues.why: Turning the toes up shifts work to the tensor fascia lata and hip flexors.

cues.cue: About 35-45° is enough.
cues.why: Lifting higher only bends the trunk sideways; the side-lying lift already gives the highest glute medius activity of common exercises.

cues.cue: Slow lift, 1-2 second hold, slow lower.
cues.why: Control keeps the side hip working through the whole rep.

families.breathing: Breathe out as the leg lifts, in as it lowers.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 second, hold 1, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Hips roll back
mistakes.looks: The top hip rolls behind the bottom one and the toes turn up to the ceiling.
mistakes.fix: Stack your hips, toes forward; lie with your back against a wall.
mistakes.why: The lift becomes hip flexion with rotation, done by the front hip muscles.

mistakes.name: Leg drifts forward
mistakes.looks: The lifting leg moves in front of the body line.
mistakes.fix: Keep the leg in line with your body or slightly behind it.
mistakes.why: A leg in front lets the hip flexors and TFL take over.

mistakes.name: Lifting too high
mistakes.looks: The leg swings high and the waist crunches sideways.
mistakes.fix: Stop at about 45° and hold.
mistakes.why: Past the hip's range the trunk side-bends to fake height.

safety: Hip pain on the side you lie on: put a pillow under it or do the standing version.
Lower-back pain: keep the trunk still and the range smaller.

variants.change: Band above the knees or at the ankles: band at the feet is harder.
Extra load on the leg: same keyframes.
Bent knee: shorter lever, easier.
Kneeling on one knee with a cable at the free ankle.
Push the knees out against a band or pad while holding a squat.

subtypes.name: Clam
subtypes.change: Side-lying with hips about 45° and knees about 90° bent, feet together; lift the top knee by turning the thigh out.

subtypes.name: Seated abduction (machine or band)
subtypes.change: Seated, hips and knees 90°, push both knees out against the pads or a band.

subtypes.name: Standing abduction
subtypes.change: Stand on one leg holding a support; move the other leg out to the side with the trunk upright.

subtypes.name: Lateral band walk
subtypes.change: Band around the legs, small half squat, step sideways keeping tension; knees stay out. Loop: cycle.

motion.basis: Default is side-lying straight-leg abduction on the left side, right leg lifting (body is horizontal; joint angles are relative to the trunk). Top height about 45° from aaos-knee; glute medius ranking from distefano2009; position faults from selkowitz2013. Angles otherwise estimated.

families.name: Hip adduction
families.pattern: Legs pull in toward the midline against resistance, seated, lying, standing or squeezing a ball.
setup: Seated machine: back on the pad, knees and hips about 90°, pads on the inside of your knees.
Start with the legs only as wide as feels comfortable in the groin.
Hold the handles and sit tall.

steps.text: Legs apart, a light stretch on the inner thighs.
Pull your knees together smoothly.
Squeeze for a moment with the pads together.
Let the legs open slowly to the start.

cues.cue: Open only as wide as you control.
cues.why: The groin is most often strained at long lengths; build range over weeks.

cues.cue: Sit tall and keep your hips on the seat.
cues.why: Leaning or lifting the hips turns the pull into a body throw.

cues.cue: Squeeze in 1 second, open in 2.
cues.why: Slow lengthening is the part that builds groin resilience.

cues.cue: Band, side-lying and ball-squeeze versions all work the adductors hard.
cues.why: Several simple adduction exercises reach high adductor longus activity.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you squeeze in, in as the legs open.

tempo.note: Squeeze in 1 second, hold 1, open in 2.

mistakes.name: Starting too wide
mistakes.looks: The legs are forced into a deep straddle at the start.
mistakes.fix: Set the machine narrower and widen it over time.
mistakes.why: A sudden heavy stretch is how adductor strains happen.

mistakes.name: Slamming the pads
mistakes.looks: The legs snap shut and the weight crashes back.
mistakes.fix: Pause when the pads meet and open slowly.
mistakes.why: Momentum skips the slow lengthening half.

mistakes.name: Hips lift or trunk leans
mistakes.looks: The hips come off the seat or the body rocks forward to help.
mistakes.fix: Sit tall against the pad and lighten the load.
mistakes.why: The hip flexors and body swing take over from the adductors.

safety: Groin pain: start with a ball squeeze at a pain-free effort and build up.
Never force the start position wider than you can control.

variants.change: Standing with a cable or band at the ankle: sweep the leg in across the standing leg.
Side-lying: lift the bottom leg 15-20 cm with the top leg crossed in front.
Squeeze a ball between the knees and hold 5-10 seconds.
Adduction pressure added to a bridge or split squat: hold the pad between the knees.

subtypes.name: Side-lying adduction
subtypes.change: Lie on your side, top leg crossed in front with the foot down; lift the straight bottom leg. Lift about 15-20 cm.

subtypes.name: Standing cable or band adduction
subtypes.change: Stand side-on to the anchor and pull the near leg in past the standing leg.

subtypes.name: Ball squeeze
subtypes.change: Lying on your back, knees bent, squeeze a ball between the knees and hold. Tracking: hold.

motion.basis: Default is the seated adduction machine. Start width estimated (machines allow about 30-50° per side); adductor exercise choice from serner2014; slow eccentric and range progression from haroy2019.

families.name: Hip flexion
families.pattern: Thigh lifts forward and up against resistance, standing or lying: the knee drive of sprinting and stair climbing.
setup: Stand tall side-on to a support, cable or band strap on the working ankle.
Standing knee soft, weight over the middle of that foot.
Brace your trunk so it will not lean back.

steps.text: Working leg slightly behind you, toes on the floor.
Drive the knee up and forward until the thigh is about level.
Hold a moment, trunk tall, toes up.
Lower the leg slowly back behind you.

cues.cue: Stay tall; do not lean back to lift the leg.
cues.why: Leaning back and tucking the pelvis lets the trunk fake the hip range.

cues.cue: Knee up to hip height.
cues.why: The iliopsoas works hardest when the thigh is lifted high.

cues.cue: Standing hip level, glute tight.
cues.why: The standing side hip holds the pelvis level for every single-leg drive.

cues.cue: Drive fast, lower slow.
cues.why: Hip flexor training has improved sprint and shuttle times; a fast drive matches running.

families.breathing: Breathe out as the knee drives up, in as it lowers.

tempo.note: Drive up in 1 second or less, hold 1, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Leaning back
mistakes.looks: The trunk tips back and the lower back rounds as the leg rises.
mistakes.fix: Brace, chest slightly forward, use less load.
mistakes.why: The spine and pelvis are making the range, not the hip flexors.

mistakes.name: Swinging the leg
mistakes.looks: The leg is kicked up and drops back with no control.
mistakes.fix: Pause at the top and take 2 seconds to lower.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the lift; the muscle only works briefly.

mistakes.name: Standing hip drops
mistakes.looks: The standing-side hip sinks or the standing knee bends a lot.
mistakes.fix: Stand tall on that leg, squeeze its glute.
mistakes.why: The side hip muscles of the standing leg are not holding the pelvis.

safety: Front-of-hip pinching: lift only to the pain-free height.
Lower-back pain: avoid the lying straight-leg version; keep the knee bent.

variants.change: Band anchored low behind you; same keyframes.
Straight-leg lift to about 45°: harder lever.
Lying on your back, pull the knee to the chest against a cable at the foot.
Fast knee drives, often alternating or after a step-up or push-up.

subtypes.name: Lying hip flexion
subtypes.change: On your back, cable at the foot; pull the knee toward the chest, other leg straight.

subtypes.name: Knee drive
subtypes.change: Explosive knee drive with the opposite arm swinging forward, like a sprint start.

motion.basis: Right leg working, left leg standing. Hip flexor role from andersson1997; joint angles estimated for a bent-knee cable hip flexion to thigh level. No kinematic study of the cable version found.

families.name: Hip thrust and glute bridge
families.pattern: Lying hip extension: shoulders on a bench or the floor, feet planted, the hips drive up until the body is straight from shoulders to knees.
setup: Sit with the bench edge just under your shoulder blades (or lie on the floor for a bridge).
Feet flat, about hip width, placed so the shins are vertical at the top.
Bar or weight over the hip crease, with a pad. Chin tucked, ribs down.

steps.text: Push through your heels and lift your hips.
Stop when shoulders, hips and knees are in a line. Shins vertical.
Hold a second and squeeze your glutes. Pelvis tucked, not arched.
Lower the hips under control until they nearly touch down.

cues.cue: Ribs down, tuck the pelvis at the top.
cues.why: The hips should finish the move; arching the low back fakes the last part of the range.

cues.cue: Shins vertical at the top.
cues.why: Feet too close shifts work to the quads; too far shifts it to the hamstrings.

cues.cue: Chin tucked, eyes forward over your knees.
cues.why: The trunk moves as one block with the hips and the neck stays relaxed.

cues.cue: Full hip extension and a short squeeze each rep.
cues.why: Glute activity is highest near full hip extension in the thrust.

cues.cue: Knees track over the toes, pushing slightly out.
cues.why: Keeps the hips in line and adds glute medius work.

families.breathing: Breathe in at the bottom, brace, breathe out as you lock out.

tempo.note: One-second squeeze at the top.

mistakes.name: Low back arches at the top
mistakes.looks: The ribs flare and the low back bends to lift the hips higher.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the chin and pelvis; stop when hips are straight.
mistakes.why: Range comes from the spine instead of the hips.

mistakes.name: Hips do not reach full extension
mistakes.looks: At the top the hips stay below the line from knees to shoulders.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load; pause and squeeze at the top.
mistakes.why: The part of the range with the most glute work is skipped.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: Knees fall toward each other as the hips rise.
mistakes.fix: Push the knees out; add a band above the knees as a reminder.
mistakes.why: Shows weak hip control and twists the knee.

mistakes.name: Feet too far out
mistakes.looks: Shins slant forward and the knees are almost straight at the top; hamstrings cramp.
mistakes.fix: Walk the feet in until the shins are vertical at the top.
mistakes.why: The hamstrings take over from the glutes.

safety: Pad the bar; bruising over the hip bones is common.
Low back pain: keep the ribs down and avoid arching at the top.

variants.change: Loaded on the hips. A barbell thrust gave more glute activity than band or American (higher bench) thrust variations.
Shoulders on the floor: shorter range at the hip. One study found more glute activity in a barbell glute bridge than a barbell hip thrust.
One foot down: about the same peak glute force as a loaded split squat.
Band above the knees: push out against it; more glute medius.
Hold the bridge and lift one foot at a time; trunk must stay level.
Feet on a bench: bigger range, more hamstrings.
One foot ahead of the other: more load on the back foot.
Short range near the top only, constant tension.
Small fast reps near the top.
Hold the top position for time.

subtypes.name: Single-leg bridge or thrust
subtypes.change: One foot planted; the other knee is held up (or the leg straight in line).

subtypes.name: Frog pump / frog hip thrust
subtypes.change: Soles together, knees wide; short range near the top.

subtypes.name: Kneeling hip thrust
subtypes.match: kneeling hip thrust|on knees|kneeling pulse|kneeling hold to stand
subtypes.change: Kneeling, band or cable from behind at the hips: sit back toward the heels, then drive the hips forward to a tall kneel.

subtypes.name: Straight-leg / hamstring bridge
subtypes.match: hamstring bridge|straight leg glute bridge|straight leg hip bridge|heel glute bridge
subtypes.change: Heels farther out, knees only a little bent: hamstrings do more of the work.

subtypes.name: Glute bridge (floor)
subtypes.match: bridge|hip raise|hip lift|low back off floor|glute march
subtypes.change: Shoulders stay on the floor; hips lift from the floor to the line from shoulders to knees.

motion.basis: Barbell hip thrust as default. brazil2021 measured joint angles (hip demand highest, hip moment falls toward the top) but numbers were not available here; angles are estimates from the setup geometry: torso horizontal (trunk -90) at the top, knee near 90 with vertical shins. EMG findings from contreras2015, contreras2016, kennedy2024, andersen2018 and neto2020.

families.name: Push press, jerk and thruster
families.pattern: Leg-driven overhead lift: a short knee dip and hard drive launch the weight from the shoulders, the arms finish it overhead.
setup: Bar on the front of your shoulders, hands just outside them, elbows a little in front of the bar.
Feet hip width, weight over the middle of the foot.
Brace hard: ribs down, glutes tight.

steps.text: Bend your knees a short way straight down, torso upright, heels flat.
Drive up hard through your legs so the bar leaves your shoulders.
Push the bar straight up as it rises, moving your head back then through.
Arms locked, bar over your ears and mid-foot, legs straight.
Lower the bar to your shoulders, softening your knees to absorb it.

cues.cue: Dip straight down, chest up.
cues.why: A forward lean in the dip sends the bar forward instead of up.

cues.cue: Short, fast dip: about a quarter of a squat.
cues.why: Overhead lifts are driven mostly by the knee; a deep or slow dip loses the stretch and the power.

cues.cue: Legs finish the drive before the arms press.
cues.why: Peak power comes from the leg drive; push press power peaks around 65-75% of a max.

cues.cue: Lock out hard, bar over the back of your head.
cues.why: A stacked lockout puts the load on bones, not on the shoulder muscles.

cues.cue: Ribs down, glutes tight overhead.
cues.why: Leaning back to finish the press arches and loads the lower back.

families.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the dip, hold through the drive, breathe out at lockout or on the way down.

tempo.note: Dip and drive are one quick bounce; lower the bar under control.

mistakes.name: Dip forward
mistakes.looks: Chest drops and hips move back in the dip.
mistakes.fix: Knees forward, torso straight up and down.
mistakes.why: The bar is driven forward and you chase it.

mistakes.name: Dip too deep or slow
mistakes.looks: Knees bend past a quarter squat and pause at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Short, sharp dip and an instant drive.
mistakes.why: It wastes the stretch-shortening response of the legs.

mistakes.name: Leaning back to press
mistakes.looks: The lower back arches and ribs flare as the bar goes overhead.
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, squeeze glutes, lighter weight.
mistakes.why: It shifts load to the lower back.

mistakes.name: Soft lockout
mistakes.looks: Elbows still bent when the bar stops overhead.
mistakes.fix: Punch up and lock out, then hold for a beat.
mistakes.why: Bent elbows overhead load the triceps and shoulder unstably.

safety: Shoulder pain overhead: use a landmine press or neutral-grip dumbbells.
Wear shoes with a firm sole; a heel lift can help in the thruster squat.
Missed jerk: push the bar forward and step back.

variants.change: Legs straight once the drive ends; the arms press to finish.
After the drive, re-bend the knees and drop under the bar to catch it locked in a quarter squat, then stand.
After the drive, split the feet: front shin vertical, back knee soft on the ball of the foot. Then step the front foot back, then the back foot in.
Drop under into a full overhead squat to catch.
Front squat to full depth, then one drive straight into the press.
One weight at a time; brace against side bend.
Bar end pressed up and forward on an arc; easier on the shoulder.
Bar on the back of the shoulders; wider grip.
Dip drill only: dip and drive, no press.

subtypes.name: Split jerk
subtypes.change: Feet split front and back under the bar in the catch.

subtypes.name: Push or power jerk
subtypes.change: Second knee bend to catch the bar locked overhead, then stand.

subtypes.name: Thruster
subtypes.change: Full front squat, then drive straight up into the press.

subtypes.name: Landmine push press
subtypes.change: One hand on the bar end at the shoulder, staggered or kneeling stance; press up and forward on an arc.

motion.basis: Dip and drive as a knee-dominant action from cleather2013a; dip and thrust phases and loads from soriano2019 and lake2014b. Dip depth (about 10% of height in coaching texts) and all joint angles are estimates, not measured values. Scapular upward rotation overhead uses the default shoulder rhythm.

families.name: Jump rope
families.pattern: Small rhythmic hops on the balls of the feet while the wrists turn the rope under you.
setup: Rope length: stand on the middle, handles reach about your armpits.
Elbows close to your sides, hands just in front of the hips.
Feet together, weight on the balls of the feet.

steps.text: Land softly on the balls of your feet, knees a little bent.
Heels stay just off the floor; ankles and knees give.
Spring up with the ankles as the rope comes under your feet.
Hop only 2-3 cm high while the wrists keep turning.

cues.cue: Balls of the feet, heels kissing the floor at most.
cues.why: Rope jumping is driven by the ankles; landing on the forefoot lets the calves and tendons absorb and return energy.

cues.cue: Just clear the rope: 2-3 cm.
cues.why: Higher hops cost more effort and land harder for no benefit.

cues.cue: Turn the rope with the wrists, elbows by your sides.
cues.why: Big arm circles slow the rope and tire the shoulders.

cues.cue: Soft knees, never locked on landing.
cues.why: Knee bend shares the landing load with the ankle.

families.breathing: Steady and relaxed; do not hold your breath.

tempo.note: About 100-140 turns a minute; one hop per turn.

mistakes.name: Jumping too high
mistakes.looks: Knees tuck up and you float well above the rope.
mistakes.fix: Hop just high enough for the rope to pass.
mistakes.why: Wastes energy and lands harder.

mistakes.name: Landing on the heels
mistakes.looks: Flat-footed thuds, heels hit first.
mistakes.fix: Stay on the balls of your feet.
mistakes.why: Heel landings send the shock up to the knees and back.

mistakes.name: Arms swing wide
mistakes.looks: Elbows lift away and the whole arm circles.
mistakes.fix: Elbows in, small wrist circles.
mistakes.why: The rope slows and the shoulders tire.

safety: Jump on wood, rubber or a mat, not concrete.
Calf or shin pain: shorter sessions, build up slowly.

variants.change: Slow, under 100 skips a minute: about 8.3 MET (15552).
100-120 skips a minute: about 11.8 MET (15551).
120-160 skips a minute: about 12.3 MET (15550).
Double unders: about 10.0 MET (15554). Higher hop (about 15-20 cm), faster wrists.

subtypes.name: Two-foot bounce
subtypes.change: Default keyframes. Side to side: hop 15-20 cm left and right.

subtypes.name: Alternate-foot step
subtypes.change: Running in place over the rope, one foot per turn; high knee version lifts the thigh to hip height.

subtypes.name: Double under
subtypes.change: Higher hop with a small knee tuck; rope passes twice per jump.

motion.basis: Forefoot landing and ankle-dominant pattern from rope2022 and rope2023 (full text not read; values not taken from them). All angles are estimates.

families.name: Jump squat, tuck and split jumps
families.pattern: Vertical jump from a quick squat dip: hips, knees and ankles extend together, then land softly and reload.
setup: Feet hip to shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Chest up, arms ready to swing (or hands on hips, or holding the load).
Weight over the middle of your feet.

steps.text: Swing your arms back and sink quickly to about a half squat.
Drive the floor away and swing your arms up; leave the ground with straight legs and pointed toes.
Land on the balls of your feet, roll to flat and bend hips and knees to absorb.
Stand tall, or go straight into the next jump.

cues.cue: Land soft and quiet, like a spring.
cues.why: Bending knees and hips at landing reduces impact; taught landers make lower forces.

cues.cue: Knees out over your toes on take-off and landing.
cues.why: Knee valgus on landing predicts ACL injury; female athletes show more of it.

cues.cue: Swing your arms hard.
cues.why: An arm swing raises jump height through several combined effects.

cues.cue: Full extension: hips, knees, ankles straight at take-off.
cues.why: The jump squat and power clean share this extension pattern.

cues.cue: Quick dip, quick jump.
cues.why: A fast stretch-shortening cycle improves power; a long pause wastes it.

families.breathing: Breathe in on the dip, out on the jump; keep breathing in fast sets.

tempo.note: Explosive. For power: 3-6 reps with full rest. For conditioning: continuous jumps in intervals.

mistakes.name: Stiff landing
mistakes.looks: Legs nearly straight at contact and a loud landing.
mistakes.fix: Land toes-to-heels and sink into the next dip.
mistakes.why: Higher impact on knees and back.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: Knees move toward each other on take-off or landing.
mistakes.fix: Spread the floor with your feet; jump lower until it is clean.
mistakes.why: Knee valgus on landing links to ACL injury.

mistakes.name: Chest collapses
mistakes.looks: The torso folds forward on landing, heels lift.
mistakes.fix: Chest up, hips back, weight mid-foot.
mistakes.why: Moves load to the lower back and toes.

mistakes.name: Uneven landing
mistakes.looks: One foot lands first or the feet land at different spots.
mistakes.fix: Jump lower and aim for one sound on landing.
mistakes.why: Asymmetric landing is a scored error in landing screens.

safety: Loaded jump squats: keep the load light (well under a third of your squat max) and land softly.
Knee or Achilles pain: switch to box jumps (lower landing force) or squats.
Plyometrics on fresh legs; stop when landings get loud.

variants.change: Holding a load: smaller jump, same landing rules.
Band under the feet resists the jump.
Holding suspension straps for help and balance.
Continuous squat jumps in intervals: about 11.0 MET (02214).

subtypes.name: Split jump
subtypes.change: Lunge stance, jump and switch legs in the air, land in a soft lunge.

subtypes.name: Tuck jump
subtypes.change: Jump high and pull both knees to the chest at the peak, then open up before landing.

subtypes.name: Pogo and calf jumps
subtypes.change: Small, fast bounces off the balls of the feet with knees nearly straight; the ankles do the work.

subtypes.name: Single-leg jump
subtypes.match: single leg|one leg|pistol|2 to 1|1 to 2|two to one
subtypes.change: Take off and land on one leg; free knee bent, much lower jump height.

subtypes.name: Jump with a turn
subtypes.change: Same jump with a turn or a change of foot position in the air.

motion.basis: Landing targets from padua2009 and herrington2010 ranges; valgus risk from hewett2005 and ford2003; arm swing from lees2004; extension pattern from mackenzie2014. Keyframe angles are estimates. Conditioning MET 7.5 is Compendium 02020 (vigorous calisthenics); interval use 11.0 (02214).

families.name: Jumping jack
families.pattern: Jump the feet out and in while the arms sweep up overhead and down to the sides.
setup: Stand tall, feet together, arms by your sides.
Weight on the balls of the feet, knees soft.

steps.text: Jump the feet just wider than the shoulders as the arms sweep up.
Land softly, knees bent, hands meet overhead.
Jump the feet back together as the arms sweep down.

cues.cue: Land on the balls of the feet, knees soft.
cues.why: Soft landings lower the impact on knees and shins.

cues.cue: Knees point the same way as the toes.
cues.why: Knees caving in on landing is a known sign of poor control linked to knee injury.

cues.cue: Arms straight but not locked, full sweep.
cues.why: The full arm range adds shoulder work and keeps the rhythm.

cues.cue: Steady rhythm you can hold for the whole set.
cues.why: Vigorous calisthenics like jacks reach about 7.5 MET.

families.breathing: Breathe in rhythm, such as out every second jump.

tempo.note: About 1 jack a second; one loop is out and in.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: Knees fall inward when the feet land wide.
mistakes.fix: Push the knees out over the toes.
mistakes.why: Inward collapse loads the knee ligaments.

mistakes.name: Stiff-legged landing
mistakes.looks: Knees locked, flat-footed thump.
mistakes.fix: Land on the forefoot and let the knees bend.
mistakes.why: Shock goes straight to the knees and back.

mistakes.name: Half arm swing
mistakes.looks: Hands stop at shoulder height.
mistakes.fix: Sweep the hands all the way overhead.
mistakes.why: Less work and broken rhythm.

safety: Low impact: step one foot out at a time (jack step).

variants.change: Vigorous calisthenics: about 7.5 MET (02020).
Step jacks, no jump: moderate calisthenics, about 3.8 MET (02022).
Done in a plank as part of HIIT: up to about 11.0 MET (02214).

subtypes.name: Plank jack
subtypes.change: In a high or forearm plank, jump the feet out and in; hips stay level.

subtypes.name: Squat jack
subtypes.change: Land wide in a squat, hands at the chest.

subtypes.name: Cross jack
subtypes.change: Arms and legs cross in front instead of meeting overhead; split jacks land one foot forward.

subtypes.name: Star jump
subtypes.change: Explosive jump to an X in the air with arms and legs wide.

subtypes.name: Step jack
subtypes.change: One foot steps out at a time, no flight. Press version pushes dumbbells overhead.

motion.basis: No kinematic study of the jumping jack found. Angles are estimates; landing cues follow general landing research (hewett2005) and NSCA convention.

families.name: Kettlebell swing
families.pattern: Ballistic hip hinge: the bell swings back between the legs, then a snap of the hips throws it forward to chest height.
setup: Feet a bit wider than hips, bell a foot in front of you.
Hinge, grab the handle with both hands, flat back.
Tip the bell toward you and hike it back between your thighs like a football snap.

steps.text: Bell goes high between the thighs, forearms touch the inner thighs, hips back.
Drive the hips forward hard; arms stay long and loose.
Stand tall like a plank; the bell floats to chest height.
Let the bell fall; hinge only when your arms meet your body.

cues.cue: Hinge, don't squat: hips back, shins nearly vertical.
cues.why: The hinge style gave more hamstring activity than squat-style swings.

cues.cue: At the top, glutes and abs tight, stand straight like a plank.
cues.why: The swing is fast on-off muscle pulses; a hard brace at the top protects the back.

cues.cue: Arms are ropes; the hips move the bell.
cues.why: Glute activity reaches about 80% of max with a 16 kg bell when the hips drive it.

cues.cue: Flat back at the bottom, neck long.
cues.why: Low back compression is about 3,200 N even with a 16 kg bell.

cues.cue: Go heavier as you get better, not faster and sloppier.
cues.why: Heavier bells raised hip and lumbar moments but not knee moments.

families.breathing: Short sharp breath out at each hip snap; breathe in as the bell drops.

tempo.note: One swing about every 1.5 seconds.

mistakes.name: Squatting the swing
mistakes.looks: Knees bend deep and push forward; the bell swings low near the floor.
mistakes.fix: Push hips back, shins near vertical; bell goes between the thighs.
mistakes.why: Turns a hip drive into a squat; less hamstring work.

mistakes.name: Lifting with the arms
mistakes.looks: The shoulders shrug and the arms raise the bell like a front raise.
mistakes.fix: Relax the arms; drive with the hips.
mistakes.why: Shoulders get tired and the hips do less.

mistakes.name: Leaning back at the top
mistakes.looks: The hips push past the feet and the shoulders lean behind them.
mistakes.fix: Finish straight: squeeze glutes, ribs down.
mistakes.why: Adds spine extension at the moment of highest speed.

mistakes.name: Back rounds at the bottom
mistakes.looks: The bell pulls the shoulders and spine forward on the backswing.
mistakes.fix: Lighter bell, hike it higher between the thighs.
mistakes.why: Loads a flexed spine at speed.

safety: Learn the deadlift hinge first.
Clear space in front and behind; stop the set with a controlled backswing and park the bell.
Back irritation: a few people find swings aggravate the back; reduce load or switch to hip thrusts.

variants.change: One hand: the opposite upper back muscles work about 24% harder to resist twisting.
Bell goes overhead: more shoulder range and more spine extension at the top.
Hold one dumbbell by the end; same pattern.
Band from behind or under the feet: no swing of a weight, the band resists the hip snap.
Bell swings in a diagonal arc across the body: more rotation.
Combination: swing into a catch at the chest, then squat or press.
No weight: arms swing to practise the hinge timing.

subtypes.name: Full / overhead swing
subtypes.change: Bell continues overhead, arms by the ears at the top.

subtypes.name: Side swing
subtypes.change: Bell swings past the outside of one hip and up across the body.

motion.basis: Hinge-style two-hand swing. mcgill2012 and vangelder2015 recorded sagittal motion but only muscle and load values were available here; joint angles are estimates of a typical hinge swing (bell to chest height, shoulderFlex about 90). MET 9.8 is the 2024 Compendium entry 02058 kettlebell swings.

families.name: Kicks
families.pattern: Strike with the leg from a guard: lift and chamber the knee, extend (or swing) the leg fast toward the target, re-chamber and land back in stance.
setup: Fighting stance: left foot forward, feet a little wider than your hips, knees soft.
Hands up in a guard, chin tucked.
Warm up hips and hamstrings before high kicks.

steps.text: Weight balanced, guard up.
Lift the kicking knee high and fold the lower leg tight.
Snap or push the foot out to the target, standing leg slightly bent.
Pull the foot back to the chamber at once.
Put the foot back down in stance, guard still up.

cues.cue: Chamber high and tight before you extend.
cues.why: Kicks are proximal-to-distal: the thigh speeds up first, then slows as the shin whips out.

cues.cue: Pivot on the standing foot for round and side kicks.
cues.why: Turning the support foot lets the hip open and rotate, adding foot speed.

cues.cue: Keep your guard up while you kick.
cues.why: Dropping the hands to balance leaves the head open.

cues.cue: Re-chamber; never snap the knee to a lock.
cues.why: Knee extension speed reaches about 700-950°/s; the hamstrings must brake it before full lock.

cues.cue: Kick at a height you can control.
cues.why: Height comes from hip mobility; forcing it costs balance and strains the hamstring.

families.breathing: Sharp breath out on each kick.

tempo.note: One kick about 0.5-1 s; train in rounds of 1-3 minutes.

mistakes.name: No chamber
mistakes.looks: The leg swings up straight like a pendulum.
mistakes.fix: Knee up first, then extend the shin.
mistakes.why: Slower, less accurate kick and more strain on the hamstring.

mistakes.name: Leaning far back
mistakes.looks: The torso falls back to get the leg up.
mistakes.fix: Lower the kick; lean only as much as you need to stay balanced.
mistakes.why: Balance and guard are lost and the kick has less force.

mistakes.name: Standing foot does not turn
mistakes.looks: Support foot stays pointing forward on a roundhouse or side kick.
mistakes.fix: Turn the heel toward the target as you kick.
mistakes.why: The hip cannot rotate and the knee twists instead.

mistakes.name: Hands drop
mistakes.looks: Arms swing down or out to balance.
mistakes.fix: Keep fists at your cheeks.
mistakes.why: Head left open; balance gets worse.

safety: Warm up first; build kick height over weeks.
On a bag, kick with the shin or ball of the foot, not the toes.
Knee pain: slow the kick and avoid snapping to full extension.

variants.change: Target work; contact changes muscle timing compared with air kicks.
Kickboxing session: about 7.3 MET (15457).
Martial arts at a moderate pace: about 10.3 MET (15430); slow novice practice about 5.3 MET (15425).
Kick combined with a squat, jump or push-up; keep the chamber.
Floor version: a hip exercise, not a strike.
Knee strike: drive the knee up and forward, pull the target down.

subtypes.name: Spinning back kick
subtypes.change: Turn your back to the target, look over your shoulder, push the heel straight back.

subtypes.name: Hook kick
subtypes.change: Leg extends past the target to the side, then the knee bends to hook the heel back across.

subtypes.name: Side kick
subtypes.change: Chamber with the knee across the body, pivot fully, push the heel straight out sideways, torso leaning away.

subtypes.name: Roundhouse kick
subtypes.change: Knee lifts and turns over as the support foot pivots; the shin or instep whips across in a horizontal arc.

subtypes.name: Axe kick
subtypes.change: Straight leg swings up high in front, then chops straight down with the heel.

subtypes.name: Knee strike
subtypes.change: Drive the knee up and forward, hips forward, hands pull down.

metrics.label: Support foot turn (round and side kicks)

motion.basis: Default loop is a rear-leg front kick (right leg). Proximal-to-distal sequence from sorensen1996 and estevan2015; back kick as hip-and-knee push from kim2011; roundhouse knee extension speed from gavagan2017; side kick from wasik2011. Joint angles are estimates from these descriptions, not measured values. METs from the 2024 Compendium (herrmann2024).

families.name: Lat pulldown
families.pattern: Vertical pull while seated: the hands pull a bar or handles from overhead down to the upper chest, shoulder blades moving down and back.
setup: Thighs locked under the pad, feet flat.
Grip the bar about 1.5 times shoulder width, palms away.
Sit tall with a slight lean back, chest up, arms straight.

steps.text: Arms straight overhead, let the shoulders rise a little to start long.
Pull your shoulder blades down first, arms still straight.
Drive your elbows down and back until the bar reaches your upper chest.
Let the bar rise under control until your arms are straight again.

cues.cue: Pull to the front, to your upper chest, never behind the neck.
cues.why: The front pulldown works the lats at least as well; behind-the-neck shifts work to the biceps and rear delt and stresses the shoulder.

cues.cue: Hands about 1.5 times shoulder width.
cues.why: Grips from 1 to 2 times shoulder width give similar lat activity; the wide grip lowered the load lifted.

cues.cue: Think 'elbows to your back pockets', not 'hands down'.
cues.why: Coached focus on the lats raised lat activity in beginners.

cues.cue: Shoulders down and away from your ears as you pull.
cues.why: Depressing and retracting the shoulder blades is how the lower and middle trapezius share the pull.

cues.cue: Small lean back, about 10-20°, then hold it still.
cues.why: Leaning back and rocking turns the pulldown into a row and uses momentum.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you pull down, in as the bar rises.

tempo.note: Pull in about 1 second, squeeze, return in 2.

mistakes.name: Behind the neck
mistakes.looks: The head drops forward and the bar comes down behind it.
mistakes.fix: Lean back slightly and bring the bar to your upper chest.
mistakes.why: It forces the shoulder into end-range external rotation with the arm raised, and offers no extra lat work.

mistakes.name: Rocking back
mistakes.looks: The trunk swings far back on every rep to drag the bar down.
mistakes.fix: Pick a lighter weight; keep a fixed small lean.
mistakes.why: Momentum and a large lean change the exercise into a row and reduce lat demand in the top range.

mistakes.name: Shoulders stay up
mistakes.looks: The arms bend but the shoulders stay hunched near the ears.
mistakes.fix: Start each rep by pulling your shoulders down.
mistakes.why: Upper-trapezius dominance replaces the lower and mid trapezius work the pull should train.

mistakes.name: Short range
mistakes.looks: The bar stops at the forehead, or the arms never straighten at the top.
mistakes.fix: Bar to the upper chest; straight arms at the top each rep.
mistakes.why: Full range lets the lats work from a long position to a short one.

safety: Shoulder pain: use a neutral grip and pull to the front only.
Hold the bar until it is back on the stack; do not let the weight snap your arms up.

variants.change: Close or neutral grip: similar lat work, a little more biceps; elbows travel close to the body.
Palms up: more biceps; the elbows finish in front of the trunk.
Hands about 2 times shoulder width: slightly less load, similar lat activity.
Behind-the-neck pulldown: not recommended; more biceps and rear delt, more shoulder stress.
One arm at a time: trunk resists side bending; the hand can turn in as it comes down.
Kneeling, standing or lying at a cable: same arm path, trunk stays tall and braced.

subtypes.name: Kneeling or standing pulldown
subtypes.change: Kneeling or standing facing a high cable or band, trunk slightly forward; same arm and shoulder-blade path.

subtypes.name: Floor pulldown
subtypes.change: Lying face up or down on the floor, arms overhead; pull the elbows down to the sides.

metrics.label: Elbow bend
metrics.good: 100-120 at the bottom, near 0 at the top

metrics.label: Bar to
metrics.good: upper chest, in front of the face

motion.basis: Grip width effects from andersen2014 and signorile2002; front vs behind-neck from sperandei2009; scapular pattern taken from the pull-up (prinold2016) and humeral-elevation data (escamilla2009), values estimated. Lean-back angle and seated hip and knee angles are coaching convention.

families.name: Lateral hops and skaters
families.pattern: Side-to-side jumping: push off one or both feet, travel sideways, and land balanced over a bent knee.
setup: Stand on your right leg, knee and hip slightly bent, chest leaning a little forward.
Left foot off the floor behind you.
Clear space of about two body widths to each side.

steps.text: Sink into your right hip and knee.
Push sideways off your right foot, swinging your arms across.
Land on your left foot, knee bent and over your toes, right foot sweeping behind.
Load the left leg and bound back to the right.

cues.cue: Land with the knee over your toes, not inside them.
cues.why: Knee valgus on landing predicts ACL injury.

cues.cue: Land soft and stick it before the next push.
cues.why: A bent-knee, controlled landing lowers impact force.

cues.cue: Sit into the hip and push out with the glute.
cues.why: Sideways jumps rely on frontal-plane hip and ankle control, not just knee bend.

cues.cue: Chest over the standing knee.
cues.why: Leaning past the foot shifts load to the inside of the knee.

families.breathing: Steady breaths; breathe out on each push.

tempo.note: For balance and power: stick each landing 1-2 s. For conditioning: continuous rhythm.

mistakes.name: Knee caves in
mistakes.looks: The landing knee falls inside the foot.
mistakes.fix: Shorter hops; push the knee out over the little toes.
mistakes.why: Raises ACL injury risk.

mistakes.name: Stiff landing
mistakes.looks: The landing leg is nearly straight and the hop is loud.
mistakes.fix: Land on the ball of the foot and sink into the hip.
mistakes.why: More impact goes to the knee and ankle.

mistakes.name: Torso tips sideways
mistakes.looks: The upper body leans far over the landing leg or away from it.
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders level, chest over the knee.
mistakes.why: Trunk lean moves load to the knee and suggests weak hip control.

safety: Start with small hops and two-foot versions.
Ankle sprain history: practise on a flat, non-slip floor and build up.
Stop when landings get wobbly or loud.

variants.change: Two feet together, hop side to side over a line, hurdle or low step.
Hops on one leg: side to side, front to back, or a square pattern.
Hops forward and back or with a foot cross; same landing rules.
Holding a ball at the chest; less arm swing.
Continuous skaters in intervals: about 11.0 MET (02214).

subtypes.name: Side-to-side hops
subtypes.match: side to side|lateral jump|hurdle|step ?box|side jump|calf side
subtypes.change: Feet together, quick hops side to side.

subtypes.name: Single-leg hops
subtypes.change: Stay on one leg; small hops in the set direction, free knee bent.

easier: two-foot side hops over a line

motion.basis: Landing rules from hewett2005, ford2003 and padua2009 (bilateral landing studies applied to single-leg landings); frontal-plane demands from lateral-ssc2010. Keyframe angles are estimates. MET 7.5 is Compendium 02020; continuous intervals 11.0 (02214).

families.name: Lateral raise
families.pattern: Shoulder abduction: straight-ish arms lift out to the sides to about shoulder height and lower again.
setup: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in.
Soft bend in the elbows, about 10-20°.
Arms a little in front of your body, about 30° (the scapular plane).

steps.text: Lift the arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows.
Stop at about shoulder height, hands level with or just below the elbows.
Lower slowly back to your sides.

cues.cue: Thumbs level or slightly up, do not pour the jug.
cues.why: Raising with the arm turned in shifts work to the rear delt and upper trap and is the empty-can position; neutral gives the most side-delt.

cues.cue: Stop at shoulder height.
cues.why: Above about 90° the shoulder must rotate out to clear the bony arch; without it the cuff can pinch.

cues.cue: Shoulders down, neck long.
cues.why: Shrugging lets the upper trap lift the weight instead of the side delt.

cues.cue: Arms slightly forward of your sides.
cues.why: In the scapular plane the shoulder blade and humerus move together with the least strain.

cues.cue: No swing: stand still, slow on the way down.
cues.why: Leaning and swinging turn the lift into momentum and load the lower back.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Light weight, slow lowering.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looks: Shoulders rise toward the ears as the arms go up.
mistakes.fix: Lighter weight, push shoulders down, stop at shoulder height.
mistakes.why: The upper trap takes over from the side delt.

mistakes.name: Swinging the body
mistakes.looks: Knees dip and the trunk rocks back to throw the weights up.
mistakes.fix: Stand still, reduce the weight.
mistakes.why: Momentum lifts the weight and the side delt does less.

mistakes.name: Pouring the jug
mistakes.looks: Thumbs turn down and the little finger leads.
mistakes.fix: Keep thumbs level or a bit up.
mistakes.why: The turned-in arm narrows the space under the shoulder bone and shifts work to the rear delt and upper trap.

mistakes.name: Raising too high
mistakes.looks: Hands go well above the head line.
mistakes.fix: Stop at shoulder height.
mistakes.why: Raising past about 90° while turned in pinches the cuff.

safety: Shoulder pain: stay below 80°, thumbs up, arms in the scapular plane.
Use light weights; the side delt has a long lever and small loads are enough.

variants.change: Cable from the opposite side: tension stays on at the bottom.
Seated: less swing possible.
Leaning or lying on your side: more load near the bottom of the arc.
Elbows bent about 90°: shorter lever, easier.
Partial reps: only the top or bottom half.
Lu raise: thumbs up, keep going overhead until the hands meet; light weight.
One arm: hold a post with the other hand for a still trunk.
Chest on an incline bench: no swing.

subtypes.name: Y raise
subtypes.change: Arms lift up and out into a Y, about 30° in front of the body line, thumbs up. Often done face down on an incline bench for the lower traps.

subtypes.name: Side-lying raise
subtypes.change: Lying on your side (floor or bench), lift the top arm from across the body up to vertical; the load is hardest at the start.

subtypes.name: Machine lateral raise
subtypes.change: Seated, pads on the outside of the arms or elbows; same arm path.

motion.basis: Scapular upward rotation scaled from the glenohumeral to scapular ratio of about 1.7:1 in the scapular plane (mcclure2001; about 28° at 90° arm elevation including a resting value of about 5°, estimate). Arm height and plane from schoenfeld2011 and mcclure2001. Shoulder rotation is neutral by design (coratella2020: neutral raise gave the most medial deltoid); with palms in at the start and no rotation the palms face down at the top, so the forearm stays at 0.

families.name: Leg curl
families.pattern: Knee flexion: the heel is pulled toward the buttocks against a load while the hip stays still.
setup: Lying machine: knees just off the pad edge, knee joint in line with the machine pivot.
Ankle pad just above the heel, not on the calf.
Hold the handles and press your hips into the pad.

steps.text: Pull your heels toward your buttocks.
Bend as far as you can without lifting your hips.
Pause for a moment.
Straighten the knees slowly, all the way, without letting the weight touch down.

cues.cue: Hips pressed into the pad.
cues.why: Lifting the hips shortens the range and lets the back help.

cues.cue: Full range: nearly straight to fully bent.
cues.why: The leg curl loads the lower part of the hamstrings more than a hinge does; use all of it.

cues.cue: Choose seated curls for size when you can.
cues.why: Seated curls (hips bent, hamstrings longer) grew the hamstrings more than lying curls in 12 weeks.

cues.cue: Foot position is up to you.
cues.why: Toes pointed or pulled up gave the same hamstring activity and gains.

cues.cue: Lower slowly, about 2-3 seconds.
cues.why: The eccentric phase builds the hamstring strength used in sprinting.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Quick curl, slow return.

mistakes.name: Hips lift off the pad
mistakes.looks: The buttocks rise as the heels come up.
mistakes.fix: Lighter weight; press the hips down and hold the handles.
mistakes.why: The hip bends to finish the rep and the hamstrings do less.

mistakes.name: Half reps
mistakes.looks: The knee never straightens or never bends past 90°.
mistakes.fix: Lower all the way, curl until the pad nears your buttocks.
mistakes.why: Part of the muscle's working range is missed.

mistakes.name: Weight drops on the way down
mistakes.looks: The legs fall back down in under a second.
mistakes.fix: Count three on the way down.
mistakes.why: Skips the eccentric work.

safety: Hamstring cramps: lighter load and stretch between sets.
Knee pain at the back of the knee: shorten the top range.

variants.change: Hips bent about 90°: hamstrings longer, more growth in a 12-week study.
One leg at a time, hip straight.
One leg at a time; even out left and right.
Lying on your back, hips lifted in a bridge, heels pull the ball or sliders in: hamstrings also hold the hips up.
Hips kept up and straight the whole time: harder.
Hold a bent-knee position for time.
Band gets harder as the knee bends.

subtypes.name: Seated leg curl
subtypes.change: Seated, hips bent; the pad pushes down behind the ankles.

subtypes.name: Standing leg curl
subtypes.change: Standing on one leg, the other heel curls up behind you.

subtypes.name: Ball / slider leg curl
subtypes.change: On your back, heels on a ball, sliders or straps; hips up, pull the heels in.

motion.basis: Lying curl default. Knee ranges are typical machine ranges, estimated; seated hip near 85-90° per maeo2021 setup. No study here measured full lying-curl kinematics.

families.name: Leg extension
families.pattern: Knee extension in isolation: seated, the lower leg swings up against resistance until the knee is straight.
setup: Sit back against the pad, knee joint in line with the machine's pivot.
Shin pad just above your ankle, toes pointing up.
Hold the handles to keep your hips down on the seat.

steps.text: Knees bent about 90°, weight just off the stack.
Straighten your knees smoothly by tightening your thighs.
Squeeze for a moment with the knee straight but not snapped.
Lower under control back to the start.

cues.cue: Line the knee up with the machine's pivot.
cues.why: A mismatched pivot drags the pad along the shin and shears the knee.

cues.cue: Hips stay down, back on the pad.
cues.why: Lifting the hips or swinging turns it into momentum, not quads.

cues.cue: Full lift to straight, slow lower.
cues.why: The quads work hardest near full extension in this open-chain move.

cues.cue: No swinging; pause 1-2 seconds at the top.
cues.why: Control keeps load on the muscle rather than the joint.

cues.cue: After knee surgery, use the range your therapist sets.
cues.why: ACL strain in this move is highest near a straight knee, so early rehab often keeps it to about 90-45° of bend.

families.breathing: Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Lift in 1 second, hold 1, lower in 2.

mistakes.name: Hips lift and swing
mistakes.looks: The hips rise off the seat and the body jerks back to throw the weight.
mistakes.fix: Hold the handles, lighten the load, lift smoothly.
mistakes.why: Momentum and hip extension replace quad work.

mistakes.name: Stops short of straight
mistakes.looks: The knee never gets past about 30° bend at the top.
mistakes.fix: Use a weight you can fully straighten and hold.
